clue.text: Saint to make holy, solemn film

explanation.definitionFit: Shallow Grave is a 1994 British thriller directed by Danny Boyle, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Cathar is sanctimoniously offering oily concoction

explanation.walkthrough: A Cathar was a member of a medieval dualist Christian sect in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a North African chilli paste made with oil, an example of an oily spicy mixture.

clue.text: The Gallic metal corroded, like the Roman

explanation.definitionFit: Latinate means derived from or resembling Latin, the language of ancient Rome, so it describes Roman style.

clue.text: Chances of dad dancing slim … to begin with

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the probabilities or likelihood that something will happen, so they are chances.

clue.text: Grand old organ on German novel

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
taken as written
a fin is the swimming organ of a fish
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A grand old German church organ is the subject of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument or body part like a liver, but here it is a fish's fin.

clue.text: Kleptomaniac craftily concealing capital

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like stolen cash, but it means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the seat of government and largest city of Ghana, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Country dancing: cure suppressing troubles

ado means fuss or bother

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country dancing' reads as one folk pursuit, but the colon splits the definition from the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American republic on the equator, so it is a country.

clue.text: Hype practically non-stop over Tyneside Olympian

indicators.note: practically means nearly but not quite, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: PR, public relations, is promotional hype
incessant means never stopping
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the north-east of England

explanation.surface: Endless media hype surrounds a sporting hero from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess Royal rode in the equestrian three-day event at the 1976 Montreal Games, making her a competitor at the Olympics.

clue.text: Amateur catered poorly, without cold bubbly

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly and comes out in a muddled order
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for amateur
taken as written, to be reduced and rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A non-professional caterer did a bad job, and nobody got a chilled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' suggests champagne, but here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aerated has had gas forced into it, so it is fizzy and full of bubbles.

clue.text: Exchange about privies to be seen as premature

parts.note: all twelve letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swapping notes about toilets might be thought too hasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Privies are outdoor toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit previous is an informal British idiom for acting too soon, so it means premature.

clue.text: In audition, one needing a coat?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its spoken sound

explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' suggests a theatre tryout but signals that a word is to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a glossy varnish brushed on in layers, so a coat of it is a finish.

clue.text: Norwegian with complaint: menu lacking cover

parts.note: IBS, irritable bowel syndrome, is a medical complaint
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' sounds like grumbling but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, author of A Doll's House, was a playwright born in Norway.

clue.text: Occasionally switch options

definitions.meaning: first meaning: intermittently, from time to time

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the two positions, against an adverbial answer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the two settings a light switch offers

explanation.surface: Every so often you change your choices.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intermittently, and literally names the two positions available on an electrical switch.

clue.text: Lords' feuds erupted in city on the Rhine

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Düsseldorf is the capital of North Rhine-Westphalia and stands on the banks of the Rhine in Germany.

clue.text: Avoid school of tuna raptly swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters float about and settle in a fresh order

parts.note: all ten letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steer clear of a shoal of fish gliding along, utterly absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a school of fish to match the tuna, but the definition is about skipping lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To play truant is to stay away from lessons without permission, so it means skipping class.

clue.text: Frank force-fed regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A man named Frank keeps being made to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a man's name but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Free and frank both describe speech that is open, candid and unrestrained.

clue.text: One bet gets you tingling

parts.note: a means one
a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: Placing a single wager gives you a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter describes a state of nervous excitement, which matches the quivering, thrilled sense of tingling.

clue.text: Topless undergarment is kind of current

indicators.note: topless means its top is gone, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece women's undergarment

explanation.surface: Underwear without a top is a current fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' hints at fashion trends but means a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular swirl of water or air running against the main flow, a type of current.

clue.text: Crazy daughter escaped

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
eluded means got away from

explanation.surface: A mad daughter has run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deluded holds false beliefs, a loose informal sense of being out of touch with reality.

clue.text: As one who adores setters may be heard to say somewhere along the Thames

indicators.note: what someone is heard to say is judged by the ear, so the sound counts

parts.note: setters are a breed of dog, so their admirer might announce affection for dogs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setters' tempts towards crossword setters, but they are gundogs. The Isle of Dogs is a former docklands area in East London, now home to Canary Wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a peninsula enclosed by a large loop of the River Thames in East London.

clue.text: Prepare for reproduction old version of Bible, omitting Genesis at beginning

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the Vulgate is the Latin translation of the Bible

indicators.note: at beginning points to just the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: An old Bible translation drops the Book of Genesis to get ready for printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' suggests copying a text, matching the Bible surface, but it is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: To ovulate is to release an egg from the ovary, which readies the body for conceiving offspring.

clue.text: Gossip from speech by Monty Python performer?

parts.note: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python comedy team
a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle comes from a lecture given by a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the performer beside the speech, so his name comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk is trivial chatter with no serious purpose, often about other people, so it is tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Number provided by Support, ringing Personnel

explanation.surface: The support desk phones the personnel department with a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like making a phone call but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is the integer between two and four, so it is a number.

clue.text: 'Policy change? Terribly untrue (mostly)!'

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so the letters come out jumbled
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, to be shortened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician protests that claims of a policy reversal are mostly false.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete reversal of a policy or position, a common political metaphor taken from driving.

clue.text: Primarily: sing crazily, absent text?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A singer improvises wildly without any words to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the first letters spell the answer, and the words describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is jazz singing with improvised nonsense syllables instead of lyrics, so it is wild vocalising without words.

clue.text: English in ground, exercising to gain experience

exercising letters are put through their paces and moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Training on an English sports field to build up know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Experience' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or be subjected to it, which is to live through it.

clue.text: Competitive clergyman getting tense

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so one piece receives the other

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A vicar with a rivalrous streak becomes anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competitive' sounds like a personality trait but describes prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-rate prices are reduced below the usual level, as competitive pricing is low enough to beat rivals.

clue.text: Wise, large QI host, British icon, is a sizzler

parts.note: a deep thinker is wise
fat means large in girth
Stephen Fry hosted the TV quiz QI
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, a national icon

explanation.surface: A clever, portly TV quizmaster and national treasure is a hot property.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a BBC panel quiz show that Stephen Fry hosted until 2016; 'sizzler' hints at a star but means a kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-fat fryer cooks food in a bath of hot oil, which makes it hiss and crackle, so it sizzles.
